title: 3.10.2 Individual PA Part 2: In Your Own Words
description: Three short-answer questions. Explain the ideas in your own words. AI-graded, summative: one submission, nothing marked on screen.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Chapter 3 Individual PA, Part 2: In Your Own Words
aiGrader.prompt:
The student answers three short-answer questions in their own words. Mark against the three criteria below. Grade strictly on correctness, generously on phrasing: these are 14-year-olds writing their own words under time pressure. Grammar and spelling are not being assessed. Each criterion is either credited, partially credited, or withheld -- say which in the feedback and why.

Question 1 -- parameter vs argument, and what a function with no return hands back (worth 4).
The taught answers (3.2.5, 3.2.11): a parameter is the name in the function's definition, a placeholder with no value until the call; an argument is the actual value handed over at the call, assigned to the matching parameter by position. A function that finishes without running a return hands back undefined. Credit the distinction and the undefined; a concrete example of either strengthens the credit.

Question 2 -- what the caller sees when a callee changes an object (worth 3).
The taught answer (3.6.2, 3.6.5): the parameter holds a copy of the reference, so the object inside and outside the function are the same object; changing a property inside is visible to the caller (mutation), while reassigning the parameter to a new object changes nothing outside. Credit any version of the reference idea; credit mutation-vs-reassignment if they bring it up.

Question 3 -- what map() gives back, and why push() is different (worth 3).
The taught answers (3.7.4, 3.3.2): map() builds and returns a NEW array, one callback result per element, and leaves the original untouched; push() adds to the end of the array it is called on and changes it. Credit the new-array-vs-changed-original distinction; the words non-mutating and mutating are welcome but not required.

Also check, without changing the marks: each answer is in the student's own words. An answer that quotes the reading verbatim is not the skill -- say so in the feedback.

rubric.title: Question 1: parameter vs argument, and the no-return case
rubric.description: Full credit 4: the distinction is right (parameter = the name in the definition, argument = the value handed over at the call) AND the no-return case is answered (undefined). Partial 2-3: one half correct, or the distinction right but the undefined case wrong. Withhold: the two terms are called interchangeable.

rubric.title: Question 2: what the caller sees when a callee changes an object
rubric.description: Full credit 3: changes inside the function are visible to the caller, and the reason is the shared reference (copy of the reference, not a copy of the object). Bonus if they contrast reassignment. Partial 1-2: visible-outside asserted without the reference reason, or the reference idea right but mutation/confusion mixed. Withhold: says the caller sees nothing unless the value is returned.

rubric.title: Question 3: map() vs push()
rubric.description: Full credit 3: map builds and returns a new array and the original survives; push changes the array it is called on. Partial 1-2: one side explained. Withhold: says both return new arrays, or both mutate.
